item.title: Dual Health and Economic Burden of Multimorbidity in Aging Populations
item.dc:creator: Wenjing Ji
Jiacheng Zheng
Suzhen Guan
Yang Liu
Xi Chen
Zhuoer Lin
Joan Costa-Font
Reshma Aziz Merchant
item.description:
Authors: Wenjing Ji, Jiacheng Zheng, Suzhen Guan, Yang Liu, Xi Chen, Zhuoer Lin, Joan Costa-Font, Reshma Aziz Merchant, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2633002
Abstract: Importance Population aging is contributing to rising multimorbidity across physical, psychological, and cognitive domains, yet global evidence integrating health and economic burdens in older adults remains limited. Objectives To quantify the global health and economic burden of multimorbidity among adults aged 60 years or older and to assess trends from 2000 to 2023. Design, Setting, and Participants This economic evaluation used observational modeling of Global Burden of Disease study 2023 estimates as health inputs and integrated them with macroeconomic, health expenditure, and population data from World Bank Open Data, the World Health Organization Global Health Expenditure Database, and United Nations population data. Health burden analyses covered adults aged 60 years or older in 204 countries and territories from 2000 to 2023, and economic burden analyses covered 180 countries and territories. Data analyses were performed from January 27 to July 22, 2026. Exposures Cross-domain multimorbidity spanning physical conditions, psychological disorders, and cognitive disorders, operationalized as 78 multimorbidity combinations. Main Outcomes and Measures The main outcomes were years lived with disability (YLDs) per 100 000 population and economic losses. All economic indicators are reported in 2021 international dollars (USD) adjusted for purchasing power parity. Joinpoint regression characterized 2000 to 2023 trends. Results From 2000 to 2023, total YLDs increased from 2367.81 (95% uncertainty interval [UI], 1067.67-4969.59) to 2941.68 (95% UI, 1252.99-6816.95) per 100 000 population, while economic losses increased from $80.10 billion (95% UI, $59.60-$104.69 billion) to $363.25 billion (95% UI, $264.04-$502.74 billion). The highest 2023 YLD rate was observed for osteoarthritis and Alzheimer disease and other dementias (369.87 [95% UI, 163.86-752.23] per 100 000 population), whereas the largest 2023 economic loss was observed for osteoarthritis and anxiety disorders ($48.51 billion [95% UI, $31.68-$76.57 billion]). The fastest-growing combination was diabetes, anxiety disorders, and Parkinson disease, with a YLD average annual percentage change (AAPC) of 3.94% (95% CI, 3.79%-4.08%) and an economic loss AAPC of 9.92% (95% CI, 9.69%-10.13%). Conclusions and Relevance In this economic evaluation of the global health and economic burden of multimorbidity among adults aged 60 years or older, multimorbidity burden increased worldwide, with economic losses growing faster than YLDs. Heterogeneity across sex, country income groups, and disease combinations, together with divergence between disability and economic burden, suggest that policy priorities for aging populations should consider both health burden and economic vulnerability.

item.title: Multiple Dimensions of Social Vulnerability and Cervical Cancer Screening Uptake
item.dc:creator: Julie Haury
Jean Baptiste Chanier
Bruno Renevier
Geoffroy Canlorbe
Simon Crequit
item.description:
Authors: Julie Haury, Jean Baptiste Chanier, Bruno Renevier, Geoffroy Canlorbe, Simon Crequit
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639570
Abstract: Importance Despite organized screening programs, persistent social inequalities undermine cervical cancer screening effectiveness in high-income countries, disproportionately affecting the most socially vulnerable women. Objectives To identify distinct social vulnerability profiles among pregnant women and examine their associations with cervical cancer screening adherence and intraepithelial lesion detection. Design, Setting, and Participants This retrospective cohort study assessed all pregnant women 25 years or older who delivered at Centre Hospitalier Intercommunal André-Grégoire, a single tertiary care maternity unit in France, between May 1, 2019, and May 1, 2025. Exposures Social vulnerability was assessed across 15 indicators spanning administrative, psychological, and violence-related domains. Multiple component analysis and hierarchical clustering on principal components identified 6 distinct vulnerability profiles. Multiple logistic regression examined associations between profiles and cervical screening inadequacy (no cervical sample within the last 3 years, including those never screened) and squamous intraepithelial lesion detection, adjusting for maternal age and body mass index. Main Outcomes and Measures Cervical screening inadequacy (primary outcome) and low- and high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion detection (secondary outcome). Results Among 18 253 women (median [IQR] age, 32.3 [29.1-36.0] years; median [IQR] body mass index, 25.9 [22.7-29.4]), 10 248 (56.1%) were up to date with screening. Six vulnerability profiles were identified. Compared with the low-vulnerability reference profile, all profiles showed increased odds of screening inadequacy: substance use and psychological vulnerability (adjusted odds ratio [AOR], 1.33; 95% CI, 1.20-1.48), migrant or linguistic barrier (AOR, 3.40; 95% CI, 3.16-3.66), psychological violence (AOR, 2.01; 95% CI, 1.75-2.32), sexual violence (AOR, 2.08; 95% CI, 1.74-2.48), and physical violence (AOR, 2.54; 95% CI, 2.19-2.95). Violence-exposed and substance use profiles also had significantly higher proportions of women with a detected intraepithelial lesion despite reduced screening participation. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study of pregnant women, distinct social vulnerability profiles were differentially associated with cervical cancer screening inadequacy; women with migration-related barriers experienced the greatest disadvantage, and violence-exposed women showed both reduced screening and elevated disease burden. These findings suggest profile-specific interventions could help reduce cervical cancer screening inequalities among socially vulnerable populations.

item.title: Storage and Disposal of Unused Prescription Opioids for Acute Pain After Emergency Department Discharge
item.dc:creator: Raoul Daoust
David Williamson
Vérilibe Huard
Jeffrey J. Perry
Justin W. Yan
Eddy Lang
Alexis Cournoyer
item.description:
Authors: Raoul Daoust, David Williamson, Vérilibe Huard, Jeffrey J. Perry, Justin W. Yan, Eddy Lang, Alexis Cournoyer, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639607
Abstract: Importance Opioid misuse is a major public health concern, and unused prescription opioids can contribute to this problem. Objective To estimate the proportion of unused opioids among patients discharged from the emergency department (ED) for acute pain, evaluate opioid storage and disposal practices, and identify factors that may motivate patients to return unused opioids. Design, Setting, and Participants This cohort study, which was a preplanned substudy of a Canadian multicenter prospective cohort study (Quantity of Opioids for Acute Pain and Limit Unused Medication Group [OPUM] study, with recruitment beginning in May 2019 and follow-up ending in January 2024), included consecutive patients aged 18 years or older discharged from the EDs of 7 hospitals in Québec and Ontario with an opioid prescription for an acute pain condition. Participants were followed up at 2 weeks and 3 months. Exposure Opioid prescription for acute pain at ED discharge. Main Outcomes and Measures The main outcomes were the proportion of participants with unused opioids at 2 weeks and 3 months after ED discharge, opioid storage practices at 2 weeks, and opioid disposal practices at 3 months. Results Of 2590 enrolled participants in the cohort, 2047 (79.0%) completed the 2-week follow-up and 1835 (70.8%) completed the 3-month follow-up. Among participants who completed the 3-month follow-up, mean (SD) age was 51.3 (15.4) years, 947 (51.6%) were male, and mean pain intensity score at triage was 7.1 (2.3) out of 10. At 2 weeks, 1521 of 1811 participants (84.0%; 95% CI, 82.2%-85.6%) reported unused opioids; 102 of 1525 (6.7%; 95% CI, 5.5%-8.1%) stored their opioids in a locked area and 393 of 1525 (25.8%; 95% CI, 23.6%-28.0%) out of reach of children or teenagers. At 3 months, 926 of 1495 (61.9%; 95% CI, 59.4%-64.4%) reported unused opioids, kept mostly for possible future pain (534 [57.7%; 95% CI, 54.4%-60.9%]) or because participants forgot or lacked time to return them (262 [28.3%; 95% CI, 25.4%-31.3%]). Only 614 of 1835 participants (33.5%; 95% CI, 31.3%-35.7%) indicated they would voluntarily return opioids to the pharmacy if prompted, while 479 (26.1%; 95% CI, 24.1%-28.2%) would not return them regardless of incentive offered. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study, 3 months after their ED visit, many participants kept unused prescription opioids at home under suboptimal storage conditions; only one-third were willing to return their opioids to a pharmacy, while more than one-fourth were not. These findings support tailoring opioid prescriptions to individual patient needs to reduce unused medication, alongside strengthening take-back networks and enhancing patient education on safe use, storage, and disposal of opioids.

Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639458
Abstract: Importance In metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC), randomized clinical trials directly comparing androgen deprivation therapy intensification using androgen synthesis inhibitors (ASIs) vs next-generation androgen receptor inhibitors (ARIs) are lacking. Objective To compare the outcomes associated with ASI vs ARI intensification therapy among patients with mHSPC in community or academic clinical practices. Design, Setting, and Participants This was a retrospective cohort study of patients diagnosed with mHSPC between February 4, 2013, and April 29, 2024, with follow-up through the July 2024 data cut, providing a median (IQR) follow-up of 25.6 (24.5-26.6) months. Patient-level data were extracted from the nationwide US-based Flatiron Health electronic health record–derived deidentified research database of community and academic practices. Patients with evidence of an mHSPC diagnosis initiating treatment with an ASI (abiraterone acetate) or ARI (apalutamide or enzalutamide) within 3 months prior to or 6 months after an mHSPC diagnosis were eligible. Patients with prior docetaxel receipt were excluded. Exposure Treatment with an ASI vs an ARI. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was overall survival (OS), defined as time in months from mHSPC diagnosis to death or censoring at last recorded activity. Results Of 3404 patients (median [IQR] age, 73 [66-80] years), 1830 received treatment with an ASI (abiraterone), and 1574 with an ARI (507 apalutamide, 1067 enzalutamide). Following inverse probability of treatment weighting, patients receiving an ARI had significantly longer OS (median, 67.9 months [95% CI, 67.5 months to not reached]) compared with patients treated with the ASI (median, 57.2 months [95% CI, 52.7-63.3 months]) (hazard ratio [HR], 0.74 [95% CI, 0.64-0.87]); P &amp;lt; .001). Results were similar in sensitivity analyses using therapy initiation as the index date (HR, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.62-0.84]; P &amp;lt; .001) and when restricted to index dates on or after December 16, 2019 (HR, 0.67 [95% CI, 0.56-0.81]; P &amp;lt; .001). The association was not modified by insurance status or socioeconomic status. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study of 3404 patients with mHSPC, treatment intensification with an ARI was associated with significantly longer OS compared with an ASI. These findings may help guide clinical treatment selection and patient counseling. However, given conflicting clinical practice data across differing database populations, only a randomized clinical trial can definitively answer this question.

item.title: Clinical Evidence on Psilocybin and Its Representation in Media Reporting
item.dc:creator: Kim Madden
Breanne Flood
Imad Kashir
Rayan Ahmad
Hiba Ali
Rotem Petranker
James MacKillop
Anthony Adili
item.description:
Authors: Kim Madden, Breanne Flood, Imad Kashir, Rayan Ahmad, Hiba Ali, Rotem Petranker, James MacKillop, Anthony Adili
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2638843
Abstract: Importance Psilocybin has received increased attention as a potential therapeutic intervention, but it is unclear whether news media reporting reflects the strengths and limitations of the clinical trial evidence. Objective To describe the annual counts of published clinical trials of therapeutic psilocybin and contemporaneous media articles and compare tone, efficacy, and safety messaging. Evidence Review This systematic review included English-language randomized and nonrandomized trials of psilocybin for clinical indications published from January 1, 2014, to October 10, 2024, and media articles describing its clinical use published from January 1, 2014, to April 22, 2025. Trials were found by searching Medline, Embase, PsycInfo, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) and were characterized by design, indication, use of psychotherapy, and reporting of efficacy and safety. Media articles were found through the Factiva database and were characterized by audience, tone, indication, efficacy claim, and safety content. Data were extracted by 2 reviewers. Risk of bias for randomized clinical trials was assessed descriptively using the Cochrane Risk of Bias tool. Findings Annual counts of both published clinical trials (n = 70) and media reports (n = 172) increased from 2018 onward. Depression was the most common clinical indication in trials (47 [67%]) and media articles (138 [80%]), while media articles frequently referenced posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) (74 [43%]) and anxiety (72 [42%]) as clinical indications despite absent and limited trial evidence, respectively, for these conditions. Overall, 49 trials (70%) reported benefit for the primary indication; 125 media articles (73%) made at least 1 positive efficacy claim, and 122 (71%) adopted a favorable tone. Trials typically described small sample sizes of less than 100 participants (65 trials [93%]) and methodologic limitations. Overall, 31 trials (44%) reported safety outcomes, with some (24 [34%]) documenting short-term adverse events, such as transient anxiety, nausea, or headache; long-term safety was rarely assessed (4 trials [6%]). Only 51 media articles (30%) mentioned safety; when harms were discussed, potential long-term psychological risks were sometimes noted (12 articles [7%]). Conclusions and Relevance In this systematic review of clinical trials and media articles, both reported positive effects of therapeutic psilocybin with similar frequency. Academic publications were more cautious and explicit about methodologic limitations, whereas media reports often presented benefits as established, extrapolated them to indications with little or no trial evidence, and provided less safety information. Clarifying these differences in emphasis may support more transparent public communication of indication-specific evidence and uncertainty as interest in psilocybin-assisted treatments grows.

item.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Perioperative Enfortumab Vedotin and Pembrolizumab for Bladder Cancer
item.dc:creator: Zhuo Tony Su
Tyler S. Garman
Carlos A. Rivera Lopez
Ruchika Talwar
Raju Chelluri
Burles A. Johnson

item.description:
Authors: Zhuo Tony Su, Tyler S. Garman, Carlos A. Rivera Lopez, Ruchika Talwar, Raju Chelluri, Burles A. Johnson, Hiten D. Patel, Akshay Sood, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2640370
Abstract: Importance Although cisplatin-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy for patients with localized muscle-invasive blader cancer (MIBC) is associated with improved survival, nearly half of these patients are ineligible for cisplatin-based chemotherapy and historically proceed to radical cystectomy (RC) without neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Perioperative enfortumab vedotin (EV) plus pembrolizumab with RC is an alternative option, but little is known about its cost-effectiveness compared with surgery alone. Objective To evaluate the cost-effectiveness of perioperative EV plus pembrolizumab for cisplatin-ineligible patients with localized MIBC. Design, Setting, and Participants This economic evaluation developed a decision-analytic Markov model that compared neoadjuvant EV plus pembrolizumab followed by RC and adjuvant EV plus pembrolizumab (intervention arm) vs RC alone (control arm). The sample consisted of simulated patients with MIBC who were ineligible for or declined cisplatin-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The model was informed by efficacy and safety data from the KEYNOTE-905/EV-303 trial, which had a median (range) follow-up of 25.6 (11.8-53.7) months. Analyses were performed between October 2025 and August 2026. Intervention The 2 treatment strategies were (1) neoadjuvant EV plus pembrolizumab followed by RC and adjuvant EV plus pembrolizumab and (2) RC alone. Main Outcomes and Measures Outcomes included life-years, quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs), and direct medical costs estimated from a Medicare payer perspective over a 10-year horizon. Incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) was assessed against a willingness-to-pay threshold of $100 000 per QALY. Scenario, 1-way, and probabilistic sensitivity analyses were conducted. Results The model consisted of 10 000 patients (age at baseline, 73 years; 77 900 males [77.9%]). Over 10 years, adding perioperative EV plus pembrolizumab to treatment was associated with increased projected survival from 4.12 to 5.63 life-years per patient, quality-adjusted survival from 3.20 to 4.51 QALYs per patient, and total costs from $317 513 to $412 160. Higher upfront perioperative therapy costs were partially offset by lower postprogression treatment costs ($12 578 per patient for the intervention arm vs $238 729 per patient for the control arm). Perioperative EV plus pembrolizumab with RC achieved an ICER of $72 460 per QALY vs RC alone and therefore represented a cost-effective treatment approach. In 1-way and scenario sensitivity analyses, the cost-effectiveness result was sensitive to alternative assumptions for key factors, including time horizon length, adjuvant therapy utilization rates, patient age, postprogression treatment mix, drug costs, and health utility before disease progression. In the probabilistic sensitivity analysis, perioperative EV plus pembrolizumab with RC had a 53% probability of being cost-effective vs RC alone at the prespecified willingness-to-pay threshold of $100 000 per QALY. Conclusions and Relevance In this economic evaluation of a simulated cohort of patients with cisplatin-ineligible MIBC, clinical trial–informed modeling suggested that adopting the perioperative EV plus pembrolizumab intervention extends overall survival and quality-adjusted survival and is likely cost-effective in the US.

item.title: Skin Toxic Effects and Survival With Enfortumab Vedotin–Pembrolizumab in Advanced Urothelial Carcinoma
item.dc:creator: Zachariah Thomas
Cindy Y. Jiang
Patrick J. Speck
Emanuele Crupi
Mohammad Jad Moussa
Adrienne Joseph
Carly Stender
Michael Glover
item.description:
Authors: Zachariah Thomas, Cindy Y. Jiang, Patrick J. Speck, Emanuele Crupi, Mohammad Jad Moussa, Adrienne Joseph, Carly Stender, Michael Glover, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639517
Abstract: Importance Skin toxic effects are a common early adverse event of enfortumab vedotin plus pembrolizumab (EVP) therapy, but its association with clinical outcomes in patients receiving first-line therapy remains uncertain. Objective To evaluate the association between treatment-emergent skin toxic effects and clinical outcomes among patients receiving first-line EVP. Design, Setting, and Participants This retrospective cohort study was performed at the University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center among adults with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma receiving first-line EVP therapy between March 3, 2022, and July 31, 2025. Skin toxic effects were used as a time-dependent exposure in Cox proportional hazards regression to account for immortal-time bias. Prespecified sequential adjustment models and 30-day landmark analyses were performed to assess the robustness of the findings. Exposure Treatment-emergent skin toxic effects (rash or pruritus) were identified from medical records. Main Outcomes and Measures Primary outcome was overall survival (OS). Secondary outcomes included progression-free survival and objective response rate (ORR). OS and PFS were measured from EVP therapy initiation to the respective event or last follow-up. ORR was evaluated among patients with a response assessment after the 30-day landmark, according to skin toxic effects status within the first 30 days. Results Among 185 patients (median age, 73 [IQR, 67-79] years; 140 [75.7%] male), skin toxic effects occurred in 98 (53.0%) at a median of 14 (IQR, 7-28) days after EVP therapy initiation. Skin toxic effects of grade 3 or higher occurred in 10 patients (5.4%). Skin toxic effects resulted in EV dose reduction in 31 patients (16.8%), treatment interruption in 20 (10.8%), and treatment discontinuation in 9 (4.9%). At a median follow-up of 17.7 (IQR, 11.3-24.2) months, Simon-Makuch curves demonstrated longer OS and PFS among all patients and longer OS among patients with visceral metastases in the skin toxic effects stratum than in the no toxicity stratum. In adjusted time-dependent Cox proportional hazards regression, skin toxic effects were associated with longer OS (hazard ratio, 0.34 [95% CI, 0.20-0.57]). The association remained consistent across sequential adjustment models and prespecified 30-day landmark analyses. In the 30-day landmark analyses, associations with PFS and ORR remained directionally favorable but were attenuated after multivariable adjustment. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study of 185 patients with locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma receiving first-line EVP therapy, treatment-emergent skin toxic effects were associated with longer OS. These findings support further prospective validation of skin toxic effects as an early clinical marker of treatment benefit and investigation of the biological mechanisms underlying this association.

item.title: A Conversation Tool to Enhance Care for People With Type 2 Diabetes
item.dc:creator: Kasia J. Lipska
Megan E. Branda
Anne W. Camp
Melissa Montosa
Rozalina G. McCoy
Victor V. Montori
Felipe Larios

item.description:
Authors: Kasia J. Lipska, Megan E. Branda, Anne W. Camp, Melissa Montosa, Rozalina G. McCoy, Victor V. Montori, Felipe Larios, Victor M. Montori
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639032
Abstract: Importance Effective interventions are needed to support the cocreation of diabetes care plans that are sensible, desirable, and feasible for the people living with diabetes (ie, care that fits). Objective To investigate whether an agenda-setting kit (ASK) added to usual primary care improves fit of care and glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D). Design, Setting, and Participants This single-center, clinician-level cluster randomized clinical trial was conducted from February 16, 2023, to July 26, 2024, with a 6-month follow-up, at a federally qualified health center in New Haven, Connecticut. Eligible clinicians were primary care physicians, nurse practitioners, and physician assistants who prescribed medication to treat patients with T2D. Eligible patients were English- or Spanish-speaking adults aged 18 years or older with T2D and hemoglobin (Hb) A 1c level greater than 8%. Patients were excluded if their clinician determined that an HbA 1c level 8% or lower was inconsistent with goals of care. Data were analyzed from November 7, 2024, to August 13, 2026. Intervention Clinicians were randomized 1:1 to the ASK plus usual primary care group (intervention group) or usual primary care only (control group). The ASK intervention consisted of 14 conversation cards about life with diabetes and its treatment. Prior to the clinical encounter, patients were asked to select 0 to 3 cards they wanted to prioritize for discussion. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was the 6-month change from baseline in illness intrusiveness measured with the Illness Intrusiveness Ratings Scale (IIRS; range: 13-91, with higher scores indicating greater intrusiveness) and HbA 1c level. Secondary outcomes included changes in treatment burden measured with the Treatment Burden Questionnaire (TBQ; range: 0-150, with higher scores indicating greater burden), diabetes distress measured with the 17-Item Diabetes Distress Scale (DDS-17; scores: indicate little or no distress [&amp;lt;2.0], moderate distress [2.0-2.9], and high distress [≥3.0]), and visit satisfaction. Results Eleven clinicians (6 [54.5%] female) were included in the trial along with 143 of their patients. The mean (SD) patient age was 56 (12) years; 87 participants (60.8%) were female and 88 (61.5%) reported Spanish as their primary language. Six-month survey data were available for 65 of 74 patients (87.8%) in the intervention group and 58 of 69 (84.0%) in the control group; data on HbA 1c level were available for 71 (95.9%) and 65 (94.2%), respectively. At 6 months, mean (SD) IIRS scores were 32.1 (15.1) and 37.1 (18.7) in the intervention and control groups (adjusted mean difference, −3.9; 95% CI, −10.4 to 2.6). The mean (SD) HbA 1c levels were 8.8% (1.8) in the intervention group and 9.1% (1.8) in the control group (adjusted mean difference, −0.2%; 95% CI, −0.9% to 0.5%). Mean (SD) TBQ scores in the intervention and control groups were 41.2 (44.8) and 46.8 (44.4) (adjusted mean difference, 1.0; 95% CI, −16.6 to 18.6), and mean (SD) DDS-17 scores were 2.0 (1.0) and 2.3 (1.0) (adjusted mean difference, −0.1; 95% CI, −0.4 to 0.2). Clinician-reported satisfaction was greater in the intervention group; patient satisfaction did not differ between groups. Conclusions and Relevance In this cluster randomized clinical trial of adults with T2D, use of the ASK with usual primary care was associated with greater clinician satisfaction but not with improvements in patients’ fit of care or glycemic control over 6 months. Larger studies should evaluate interventions that not only identify patients’ priorities and treatment burdens but also better support clinicians in addressing them. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT05553912

item.title: Concentrated Exposure Therapy vs Internet-Based Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
item.dc:creator: Lena Jelinek
Lara Wille
Jakob Scheunemann
Luisa Tegtmeier
Holger Zapf
Franziska Miegel
Lea Schuurmans
Josephine Schultz
item.description:
Authors: Lena Jelinek, Lara Wille, Jakob Scheunemann, Luisa Tegtmeier, Holger Zapf, Franziska Miegel, Lea Schuurmans, Josephine Schultz, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639281
Abstract: Importance Given the high prevalence, chronicity, and associated disability of obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD), optimizing treatment is a global priority. The Bergen 4-day treatment (B4DT), a concentrated exposure-based intervention, may reduce treatment burden and improve access to evidence-based care. Objective To evaluate the efficacy of B4DT compared with internet-based cognitive behavioral therapy (iCBT) in reducing OCD symptom severity. Design, Setting, and Participants Single-center randomized controlled trial (1:1 allocation). Between May 8, 2024, and August 8, 2025, adults (aged 18 to 72 years) with OCD were enrolled and were followed up for 3 months. Key exclusion criteria included schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, acute suicidality, substance dependence, and recent psychopharmacological changes. Outcomes were assessed at baseline, 6 weeks, 8 weeks (posttreatment), and 3 months (follow-up) by masked evaluators. Interventions Patients were randomized to B4DT (including preparatory sessions) or an 8-week unguided iCBT program. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was the change in OCD symptom severity, measured by the Yale-Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale (Y-BOCS). Secondary outcomes included self-reported OCD (OCI-R), dysfunctional cognitions, quality of life, depressive symptoms, experiential avoidance, global functioning, self-esteem, and treatment satisfaction. Results A total of 253 individuals were screened, and 119 were enrolled after 53 were found to be ineligible and 81 declined to participate. Sixty of the 119 randomized participants (mean [SD] age, 33.5 [10.1] years; 79 [66.4%] women) were assigned to B4DT and 59 to iCBT. The primary analysis included all randomized participants (intention-to-treat). B4DT was associated with significantly greater reductions in OCD symptoms (Y-BOCS) than iCBT, with large effects at posttreatment (mean [SE] difference, −7.9 [0.9]; 95% CI, −9.7 to −6.0; Hedges g , −1.6) and sustained effects at 3-month follow-up (mean [SE] difference, −5.6 [1.1]; 95% CI, −7.8 to −3.4; Hedges g , −1.0). Secondary outcomes consistently favored B4DT. Response and remission rates at 3-month follow-up were higher with B4DT (35 of 57 [61.4%] vs 11 of 44 [25.0%] and 24 of 57 [42.1%] vs 6 of 44 [13.6%], respectively). Conclusions and Relevance In this randomized clinical trial of 119 adults with OCD, B4DT was superior to iCBT in reducing OCD symptom severity, with sustained benefits. Its brief, concentrated format may represent a scalable strategy to improve access to effective OCD treatment globally. Trial Registration German Clinical Trials Register: DRKS00034236

item.title: Mortality Among People With Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder
item.dc:creator: Lucy Corrigan
Lauren Heywood
Gavin R. Stewart
Elizabeth O’Nions
Henry Shelford
Joshua Stott
Amber John
item.description:
Authors: Lucy Corrigan, Lauren Heywood, Gavin R. Stewart, Elizabeth O’Nions, Henry Shelford, Joshua Stott, Amber John
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639448
Abstract: Importance Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is associated with adverse life outcomes and increased mortality. Clarifying the magnitude of mortality risks using international data and the potential association between medication and mortality is essential to inform clinical care and motivate public health strategies to address mortality. Objectives To examine the association between ADHD and all-cause and cause-specific mortality and to assess whether mortality risk differs according to ADHD medication use. Data Sources A comprehensive search of PubMed, Web of Science, PsycINFO, EMBASE, MEDLINE, and CINAHL was conducted from database inception to July 8, 2025. Study Selection Eligible studies included quantitative research across all age groups reporting all-cause and/or cause-specific mortality in individuals with ADHD, defined via diagnostic criteria, self-identification, trait measures, or ADHD polygenic risk scores. Exclusion criteria were nonoriginal research, qualitative studies, non–peer-reviewed publications, and studies not reporting mortality outcomes. Data Extraction and Synthesis Data extraction was conducted independently by 2 reviewers. Study quality was assessed by 1 reviewer. Summary data were extracted from published reports, and pooled hazard ratios (HRs) were calculated using random-effects model meta-analysis. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and cause-specific mortality (suicide, unintentional or intentional injury, and natural causes), measured using HRs with 95% CIs. Results Nineteen studies including 15 920 970 participants (36.1% female) were included. ADHD was associated with increased all-cause mortality (HR, 1.71; 95% CI, 1.31-2.24; P &amp;lt; .001). Significant associations were also observed for suicide (HR, 1.89; 95% CI, 1.21-2.95; P = .005), unintentional or intentional injury (HR, 1.55; 95% CI, 1.22-2.00; P &amp;lt; .001), and natural-cause mortality (HR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.16-1.38; P &amp;lt; .001). ADHD medication use in people with ADHD was associated with reduced all-cause mortality (HR, 0.75; 95% CI, 0.64-0.87; P &amp;lt; .001). Substantial heterogeneity was observed across studies. Conclusions and Relevance In this systematic review and meta-analysis of ADHD and mortality, ADHD was associated with increased mortality across multiple causes; and ADHD medication was associated with a decreased all-cause mortality risk, underscoring the importance of timely diagnosis and treatment. However, the heterogeneity observed across studies highlights the need for standardized methods and improved control of confounding factors to better characterize mortality risk among individuals with ADHD.

item.dc:creator: Eric C. Blackstone
Yating Wang
Eno-Abasi Inyang
Andrew G. Shuman
Michael Casey
Gregory A. Abel
Andrew Hantel
item.description:
Authors: Eric C. Blackstone, Yating Wang, Eno-Abasi Inyang, Andrew G. Shuman, Michael Casey, Gregory A. Abel, Andrew Hantel
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2633164
Abstract: Importance Cancer drug shortages require health systems to rapidly develop and enact allocation policies, yet little is known about how such policies perform in practice. Objective To evaluate clinical implementation of a formal allocation policy during the 2023 carboplatin shortage. Design, Setting, and Participants This cohort study comprised a carboplatin shortage at a 7-site health system in Massachusetts and New Hampshire that lasted from June 1 to July 17, 2023. Patients with cancer who were eligible for carboplatin during the shortage were assigned priority categories using predetermined criteria based on treatment intent, inferior or contraindicated alternative treatments, clinical trial participation, and ongoing vs new treatment; these categories were assigned collectively by clinical groups and disease-specific pharmacists after a training session. A structured process conducted between September and November 2025 was used to review medical records and independently reassign categories post hoc. Exposure Allocation of carboplatin during the shortage vs mandate to switch to an alternative treatment. Main Outcomes and Measures Main outcomes were concordance between actual and review-based priority category assignments, actual allocation, and independent review–based allocation, as well as associations of demographic and clinical variables with allocation. Descriptive statistics and multivariable logistic regression assessed actual and review-based outcomes. Results Allocation decisions were made for 483 patients (median age, 66 years [IQR, 58-73 years]; 354 women [73%]). A total of 222 patients (46%) were allocated carboplatin and 261 (54%) were not. An independent review agreed with 56% of priority category assignments (189 of 335) and 74% of allocation decisions (357 of 483); 26% of allocation decisions (126 of 483) were not aligned with policy intent. Incomplete documentation (51% [74 of 146]) and treatment contraindication discrepancies (21% [31 of 146]) were the most common causes of disagreement. In multivariable regression, male gender (vs female gender; odds ratio [OR], 2.72 [95% CI, 1.26-5.99]; P = .01) and treatment at main campus (vs regional campuses; OR, 2.13 [95% CI, 1.30-3.45]; P &amp;lt; .001) were associated with increased likelihood of receiving carboplatin. In models of policy-concordant allocation based on independent review, these associations were not significant (male gender: OR, 1.39 [95% CI, 0.16-13.08]; P = .77; treatment at main campus: OR, 1.47 [95% CI, 0.33-7.14]; P = .61). Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study of allocation policy implementation during a chemotherapy shortage, most allocation decisions aligned with policy intent, but key implementation gaps were identified and may have been associated with biases in allocation. Explicit documentation, contemporaneous monitoring, and enforcement mechanisms may improve policy implementation during oncology drug shortages.

item.title: Home Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation With Gamified Cognitive Control Training for Depression

item.description:
Authors: Esther Dechantsreiter, Frank Padberg, Yuval Benjamini, Stephan Goerigk, Linda Rubene-Kesele, Liene Konosonoka, Ulrike Vogelmann, Tamar Cohen, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639400
Abstract: Importance Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) has emerged as a home-based treatment in major depressive disorder (MDD), although its effects are typically small to moderate and inconsistently observed. Because tDCS may act synergistically with behavioral interventions, combining both approaches represents a promising strategy for developing more effective home-based treatments for MDD. Objective To investigate the feasibility, safety, and efficacy of home-based tDCS and concurrent gamified cognitive control training (CCT) in adults with MDD. Design, Setting, and Participants This multicenter, double-masked, parallel-group, randomized clinical trial with follow-up at week 10, masking checks at 2 time points, and expectancy assessments was conducted at 3 university hospitals in Latvia, Germany, and Israel between June 22, 2021, and August 8, 2024. Participants included adults aged 18 to 65 years with MDD, 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale scores of at least 13, and no or stable antidepressant medication. Intervention Participants were randomly assigned 1:1 to active tDCS (2 mA; anode F3, cathode F4) plus a gamified CCT or sham tDCS plus a sham game. Participants were asked to complete 30 home treatment sessions (30 minutes each) over 6 weeks with software-assisted electrode positioning. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was feasibility, defined as completing at least 20 of 30 sessions with greater than 50% probability. The secondary outcome was efficacy, measured as change in Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) scores from baseline to week 6. Results Of 111 enrolled participants, 109 were included in the modified intention-to-treat sample (55 in the active group and 54 in the control group; mean [SD] age, 33.1 [10.6] years; 69 female [63.3%]). Feasibility criteria were met, with 86 participants (78.9%) completing at least 20 sessions (lower bound of 1-sided 95% CI, 71.5%). The MADRS scores improved significantly in both groups at week 6, indicating insufficient evidence to reject the null hypothesis of no difference in the mean change in MADRS score from baseline to 6 weeks between the 2 treatment groups (difference, 0.89 [95% CI, −1.37 to 3.15]; P = .44; Cohen d , 0.10 [95% CI, −0.15 to 0.34]). Results were similar at follow-up (week 10). Adverse events were balanced between groups. Conclusions and Relevance This RCT of home-based tDCS combined with CCT in adults with MDD was feasible and safe but did not demonstrate superior efficacy over the control condition. Future studies should refine the mechanistic alignment between stimulation and cognitive interventions to optimize treatment effects. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04953208

item.title: Timeliness of Emergency Care for Intracerebral Hemorrhage Compared With Acute Ischemic Stroke
item.dc:creator: Regina Royan
Uchechukwu Ikeaba
Brooke Alhanti
Brian Stamm
Brian Mac Grory
Shyam Prabhakaran

item.description:
Authors: Regina Royan, Uchechukwu Ikeaba, Brooke Alhanti, Brian Stamm, Brian Mac Grory, Shyam Prabhakaran, Matthew B. Maas, Gregg C. Fonarow, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639429
Abstract: Importance Clinical data comparing time to presentation and stroke quality metrics for intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and acute ischemic stroke ( AIS ) are limited. Understanding these differences is essential to provide timely care to all stroke subtypes. Objective To compare prehospital and emergency department (ED) process quality metrics between patients with ICH and AIS. Design, Setting, and Participants Cohort study included patients with AIS and ICH admitted to Get With The Guidelines (GWTG)–Stroke participating hospitals from January 1, 2015, to June 30, 2024, who arrived by emergency medical services (EMS). Data were analyzed from 195 hospitals across the US. Main Outcomes and Measures Prehospital-based and ED-based process metrics (eg, EMS prenotification, door to ED physician assessment time, door to initial brain imaging order) were assessed. Logistic and linear regression models were sequentially adjusted for patient demographics, medical history and presenting factors, and hospital characteristics. Temporal trends of prehospital care metrics were examined. Results A total of 195 659 patients (median [IQR] age, 74.0 [63.0-83.0] years; 97 978 [50.1%] female; 31 464 with ICH and 164 195 with AIS) from 195 hospitals were included. The median (IQR) National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score was 14 (6-23) for ICH vs 6 (2-13) for AIS (absolute standardized difference, 0.694). ICH (vs AIS) was associated with higher odds of door-to-ED physician assessment of 10 or fewer minutes after adjusting for patient demographics (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.08; 95% CI, 1.02-1.14). This association reversed after adding adjustment for medical history and presenting factors (including NIHSS) and hospital characteristics (aOR, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.89-0.99). This pattern was observed for door to initial brain imaging order of 20 or fewer minutes (demographic-adjusted: aOR, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.02-1.16; fully adjusted with medical history and hospital characteristics: aOR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.85-0.97). Median last known well to arrival time increased by 32.5% for AIS (151 to 200 minutes; P &amp;lt; .001) and 34.3% for ICH (108 to 145 minutes; P &amp;lt; .001), while rates of EMS prenotification largely remained stable for both ICH and AIS. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study of patients with acute stroke, patients with ICH arrived at the ED faster but were less likely to achieve care targets. In the context of emerging hyperacute ICH therapies and bundled care models, addressing these differences is essential to optimizing acute stroke outcomes.

item.title: Initial Treatment for Acute Low Back Pain and Risk of Opioid Use Disorder and Overdose
item.dc:creator: Lisa V. Doan
Anton M. Hung
Mark Olfson
Nicholas T. Williams
Kara E. Rudolph
item.description:
Authors: Lisa V. Doan, Anton M. Hung, Mark Olfson, Nicholas T. Williams, Kara E. Rudolph
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639420
Abstract: Importance Guideline-discordant care for acute low back pain (aLBP) is common and has been associated with adverse outcomes. Objectives To estimate the incidence of new opioid use disorder (OUD) or overdose diagnosis among opioid-naive patients with Medicaid coverage initiating treatment for aLBP and to evaluate the association between initial treatment modalities and subsequent risk of OUD or overdose diagnosis. Design, Setting, and Participants This retrospective cohort study used data from January 1, 2016, to December 31, 2019, with 13 months of follow-up (1-month exposure assessment followed by 12 months of outcome follow-up) from the Transformed Medicaid Statistical Information System Analytic Files from 25 states that expanded Medicaid under the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act by 2014. Participants included opioid-naive, adults aged less than 65 years who received pain treatment within 1 month of diagnosis of aLBP. Data were analyzed from March 1, 2025, to July 31, 2026. Exposures Initial pharmacologic and nonpharmacologic treatments for aLBP. Main Outcomes and Measures OUD or overdose diagnosis, defined using diagnostic codes for opioid abuse, opioid dependence, opioid-involved overdose, or a prescription for medication for treating OUD. Results In this cohort of 399 500 Medicaid patients who initiated treatment for newly diagnosed aLBP, the median age was 39 (IQR, 30-50) years, and 237 846 (59.5%) were female. The cumulative incidence of OUD or overdose diagnosis was 1.4% at 7 months and 2.3% at 13 months. Initiating vs not initiating higher-dose opioids ( &amp;gt; 50 mg of morphine equivalent) as part of the initial treatment was associated with the greatest risk, increasing risk of OUD or overdose by 146.6% (95% CI, 121.5%-171.7%). Initiating vs not initiating lower-dose opioids prescribed for more than 7 days or gabapentinoids each increased risk by 105.2% (95% CI, 89.0%-121.4%) and 101.6% (95% CI, 84.9%-118.2%), respectively. Nonpharmacologic, noninterventional therapies were associated with reductions in risk of OUD or overdose diagnosis. Initiating vs not initiating chiropractic care was associated with the largest relative risk reduction, decreasing risk by 32.8% (95% CI, 26.8%-38.9%), and initiating physical therapy was associated with 31.1% decreased risk (95% CI, 22.1%-40.1%). Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study, nonpharmacologic, noninterventional treatment was associated with reductions in risk of OUD or overdose diagnosis while initiating treatment with opioids or gabapentinoids was each associated with higher risks. These results support guideline recommendations favoring nonpharmacologic treatments as first-line therapy for aLBP.

item.title: Homicide Mortality Among Female Adolescents and Women Aged 15 to 44 Years and US State Abortion Policies
item.dc:creator: Liana R. Woskie
Maeve E. Wallace
item.description:
Authors: Liana R. Woskie, Maeve E. Wallace
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2638986
Abstract: Importance Homicide is a leading cause of death among female adolescents and women aged 15 to 44 years (hereinafter, women of reproductive age) in the US. Whether homicide trajectories differed across state abortion policy environments after the COVID-19 surge and the Dobbs v Jackson Women’s Health Organization (hereinafter, Dobbs ) decision is unclear. Objectives To characterize national homicide trends among women of reproductive age and assess whether post-2022 trajectories in homicide mortality among women of reproductive age diverged between states with and without sustained abortion bans. Design, Setting, and Participants This quasi-experimental study used national interrupted time series and comparative interrupted time series analyses of homicide mortality from January 1, 2016, through December 31, 2024, among women of reproductive age. Exposure The COVID-19 pandemic and sustained state abortion bans after Dobbs . Main Outcomes and Measures The main outcome was monthly homicide deaths. The population-offset Poisson model estimated differential post- Dobbs changes in homicide rates. Absolute rate differences, excess deaths, and years of life lost were estimated from fitted and counterfactual Poisson models. States with sustained total or near-total abortion bans after Dobbs were compared with states without such bans; states with partial or legally fluid restrictions were excluded. A triple-difference analysis comparing those aged 15 to 29 years with those aged 45 to 59 years served as a negative-control analysis. Results The analysis included 19 118 homicide deaths among women of reproductive age. Nationally, homicide increased sharply during the COVID-19 surge and subsequently decreased, with no clear national level or slope change beginning in July 2022. In policy-stratified analyses, however, homicide trajectories diverged. After July 2022, the exposed states (those with total or near-total abortion bans) vs unexposed states homicide monthly rate ratio (RR) was 1.006 (95% CI, 1.000-1.011; P = .03). Across calendar years 2023 and 2024, the fitted homicide rate in exposed states was higher than the modeled counterfactual (2023: RR, 1.07; 95% bootstrap interval, 1.01-1.13; and 2024: RR, 1.15; 95% bootstrap interval, 1.03-1.29). This corresponded to an estimated 48 excess deaths (95% bootstrap interval, 11-81) in 2023 and 87 excess deaths (95% bootstrap interval, 20-149) in 2024. A triple-difference model indicated greater post- Dobbs divergence among those aged 15 to 29 years than those aged 45 to 59 years (monthly ratio of RRs, 1.017; 95% CI, 1.000-1.034; P = .046); placebo Dobbs dates yielded nonsignificant results. Conclusions and Relevance In this study, national homicide mortality rates among women of reproductive age returned toward prepandemic levels after COVID-19, but post-2022 trajectories diverged across state abortion policy environments. The findings suggest that national improvements in homicide mortality rates among women of reproductive age may mask less-favorable homicide trends among women of reproductive age in states with sustained abortion bans.

item.title: Clinical Decision Support for Fall Prevention in Primary Care
item.dc:creator: Nancy K. Latham
Erin Hommel
Mackenzie Kiesman
Stuart R. Lipsitz
David W. Bates
Diane L. Carroll
Alexandra C. Frost
Pamela M. Garabedian
item.description:
Authors: Nancy K. Latham, Erin Hommel, Mackenzie Kiesman, Stuart R. Lipsitz, David W. Bates, Diane L. Carroll, Alexandra C. Frost, Pamela M. Garabedian, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639240
Abstract: Importance Falls are a leading cause of injury among older adults. Although exercise reduces fall risk, implementation in primary care remains limited. Objective To assess whether an electronic health record–integrated clinical decision support intervention, Electronic Strategies for Tailored Exercise to Prevent Falls (eSTEPS), reduces falls among older primary care patients at increased risk. Design, Setting, and Participants This matched-pair cluster randomized clinical trial was conducted from June 9, 2023, to May 8, 2025, with 12 to 23 months of follow-up at primary care practices within an integrated health system in the US. Adults aged 65 years or older with a positive 3-item fall-risk screen at a primary care visit were included. Intervention eSTEPS decision support embedded in the electronic health record with tailored exercise recommendations, optional physical therapy referral, and patient-facing materials (handouts, website, and app). Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was the rate of patients with 1 or more falls identified using electronic health record–derived International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision ( ICD-10 ) diagnostic codes. Secondary outcomes were the rate of patients with 1 or more fall-related injuries identified by validated ICD-10 algorithms and mortality. Results Among 11 945 participants (mean [SD] age, 77.05 [7.43] years; 8044 females [67.3%]), of whom 5681 (47.6%) were in the intervention group and 6264 (52.4%) were in the control group, at 22 primary care practices, the rate of 1 or more ICD-10 –coded falls (including falls with injuries) per 100 patient-years over the study period was 19.3 (95% CI, 18.6-20.1) in patients from intervention practices vs 21.2 (95% CI, 20.2-22.1) in patients from control practices (rate ratio [RR], 0.91 [95% CI, 0.88-0.95]; P &amp;lt; .001). The rate of ICD-10 –coded fall-related injuries per 100 patient-years was 15.7 (95% CI, 15.0-16.5) from intervention practices vs 16.7 (95% CI, 16.1-17.4) from control practices over the study period (RR for fall injuries per 100 patient-years, 0.94 [95% CI, 0.90-0.97]; P = .001). No differences were observed in mortality. For intervention patients, eSTEPS exercise prescriptions were issued for 1255 patients (22.1%). Overall, 215 clinicians (77.9%) in intervention practices used the clinical decision support to deliver the exercise program at least once over the study period. Conclusions and Relevance In this cluster randomized clinical trial of an electronic health record–integrated decision support, falls and fall-related injuries were modestly reduced in older adults in primary care. These results suggest support for scalable, workflow-integrated fall prevention. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04993781

item.title: Preterm Risk Factors, Epigenetic Age, and Neurodevelopmental Outcomes
item.dc:creator: Rhandi Christensen
Chaini Konwar
Beryl C. Zhuang
Julia MacIsaac
Vann Chau
Mehmet N. Cizmeci
Linh G. Ly
Ting Guo
item.description:
Authors: Rhandi Christensen, Chaini Konwar, Beryl C. Zhuang, Julia MacIsaac, Vann Chau, Mehmet N. Cizmeci, Linh G. Ly, Ting Guo, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639409
Abstract: Importance Studies examining biological factors associated with neurodevelopment in the preterm population are limited. It was previously demonstrated that epigenetic age acceleration was associated with better neurodevelopmental outcomes among children born preterm. It is unclear whether this association is modified by clinical and environmental preterm risk factors. Objective To examine whether the association between epigenetic aging and neurodevelopmental outcomes is modified by preterm brain injury and socioeconomic status. Design, Setting, and Participants This was a prospective cohort study of children born at 24 to 32 weeks’ gestation, recruited from 2 neonatal intensive care units from 2015 to 2019 and followed up to January 2026. The cohort was well characterized with clinical data, brain magnetic resonance imaging, and neurodevelopmental assessments (Bayley-III cognitive and motor domains) at 3 years. Participants with buccal epithelial cell DNA collected at 3 years were included. Exposure Epigenetic age (in weeks) at 3 years was determined using the pediatric buccal epigenetic clock and corrected for chronological age to give epigenetic age difference. Main Outcomes and Measures Primary analyses used linear regression to examine the association between epigenetic age difference, preterm risk factors (any brain injury, severe brain injury, maternal educational level), and cognitive and motor outcomes at 3 years. Secondary analyses examined whether brain injury and maternal education level modified the associations between epigenetic age difference and cognitive and motor outcomes at 3 years. Results A total of 102 study participants (median gestational age, 27.0 weeks [IQR, 25.6-28.9 weeks]; 54 female [53%]) were included. Higher maternal educational level (β = 11.65; 95% CI, 3.55-19.76; P = .005) and epigenetic age acceleration (β = 0.07; 95% CI, 0.01-0.14; P = .04) were associated with higher cognitive scores. Epigenetic age acceleration was also associated with higher motor scores (β = 0.16; 95% CI, 0.06-0.27; P = .003), while extreme prematurity (β = –5.66; 95% CI, −10.85 to −0.46; P = .03) and severe brain injury (β = –10.99; 95% CI, −21.32 to −0.66; P = .04) were associated with lower motor scores. Severe brain injury modified the association between epigenetic aging and motor outcomes (β = 0.41; 95% CI, 0.08-0.74; P = .02), and children with epigenetic age acceleration in the presence of severe brain injury had higher motor scores. Conclusions and Relevance In this prospective preterm cohort study, epigenetic aging, severe brain injury, and socioeconomic status were associated with neurodevelopmental outcomes. Children with severe brain injury along with epigenetic age acceleration had higher motor scores. These findings suggest the association between epigenetic aging and neurodevelopment is context dependent and can vary based on the presence of preterm risk factors.

item.title: Substance Misuse Prevalence and Risk Factors in Adolescents and Young Adults With Depression
item.dc:creator: Michael S. Toce
John J. Porter
Jamie K. Lim
Florence T. Bourgeois
item.description:
Authors: Michael S. Toce, John J. Porter, Jamie K. Lim, Florence T. Bourgeois
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639343
Abstract: Importance The prevalence of youths with mental health conditions has increased in recent years. Youths with mental health conditions are at risk of substance misuse via coping and self-regulation pathways; there is therefore a need to identify and address barriers to integrated mental health and substance use treatment in these youths. Objective To examine the prevalence of and motivations for prescription psychotherapeutic drug misuse among youths with and without depression. Design, Setting, and Participants A cross-sectional analysis of the 2023 and 2024 National Survey on Drug Use and Health (NSDUH) using a nationally representative survey of noninstitutionalized individuals aged 12 years and older related to drugs of misuse and mental health disorders. Data on adolescents and young adults were analyzed from January to March 2026. Exposure Past-year major depressive episode (MDE). Main Outcomes and Measure The primary outcome was past-year prescription psychotherapeutic drug misuse and use disorder, and the secondary outcome was motivations for misuse. Survey-weighted prevalence estimates with 95% CIs were calculated and group differences were assessed using χ 2 tests. To assess the association between drug misuse and depression, logistic regression models were used. Results The 2023 and 2024 NSDUH included 22 906 adolescents (aged 12-17 years) and 27 723 young adults (aged 18-25 years), among whom 24 831 (49.1%) were males, 13 256 (26.2%) were Hispanic, 6923 (13.7%) were non-Hispanic Black, 23 114 (45.6%) were non-Hispanic White, and 7336 (14.5%) were non-Hispanic–all other races. A past-year MDE was reported by 16.3% (95% CI, 15.6%-17.0%) of respondents, corresponding to an estimated 9.8 million individuals nationally. Among youths with a past-year MDE, 6.6% (95% CI, 5.8%-7.5%) reported misuse of psychotherapeutic drugs while 6.0% (95% CI, 5.2%-6.9%) reported use disorder. Youths with a past-year MDE had significantly higher odds of reporting prescription drug misuse (odds ratio [OR], 2.09; 95% CI, 1.75-2.50) and prescription drug use disorder (OR, 4.02; 95% CI, 3.37-4.80) compared with those without a past-year MDE. Compared with youths without a past-year MDE, youths with a past-year MDE were more likely to report misusing opioid analgesics (10.2% [95% CI, 6.4%-15.9%] vs 3.7% [95% CI, 2.2%-6.3%]; P = .01) and tranquilizers (29.8% [95% CI, 21.1%-40.3%] vs 13.2% [95% CI, 5.8%-19.9%]; P = .003) to help with feelings and emotions. Conclusions and Relevance This cross-sectional analysis of the 2023 and 2024 NSDUH found that youths with depression were more likely than their peers without depression both to report prescription drug misuse and to meet criteria for prescription drug use disorder. For certain medications, this misuse was more often motivated by a desire to address feelings and emotions. These findings underscore the need to identify and address barriers to integrated mental health and substance use treatment for at-risk youths before patterns of self-medication progress to enduring substance use disorders.

item.title: Cervical Cancer Screening Rates by Race and Ethnicity, Age, Language, and Census Region
item.dc:creator: Yunbo Xie
Linh Nguyen
Yen-Chi Le
Abigail Zamorano
item.description:
Authors: Yunbo Xie, Linh Nguyen, Yen-Chi Le, Abigail Zamorano
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639938
Abstract: Importance Longitudinal evidence of cervical cancer screening (CCS) trends before and after COVID-19 across demographic cohorts remains limited. Objective To examine CCS rates by race and ethnicity, age, language, and census region among patients with at least 1 health care encounter in an electronic medical record (EMR) system from 2019 through 2024, and to evaluate longitudinal trends across these groups. Design, Setting, and Participants Using an EMR database, this cross-sectional study evaluated CCS rates among female patients aged 21 to 64 years between 2019 and 2024, stratified by race and ethnicity, age, language, and census region. Exposures Race and ethnicity, age, language, and census region. Main Outcomes and Measures Descriptive statistics were used to summarize annual CCS rates across demographic groups. The Cochran-Armitage test assessed linear trends over time. Results Annual sample sizes ranged from approximately 9 to 16 million patients and increased steadily over time; analytic population sizes varied across subgroups. Most patients were non-Hispanic White, aged 30 to 49 years, English-speaking, and resided in either the South or Northeast. Non-Hispanic White patients had the highest annual CCS rates from 2019 to 2021 but experienced the smallest percentage increase, from 10.98% (95% CI, 10.96%-11.01%) to 13.85% (95% CI, 13.82%-13.87%), over the study period. Hispanic patients experienced the largest percentage increase in CCS rates, from 9.85% (95% CI, 9.80%-9.90%) to 15.51% (95% CI, 15.47%-15.55%). American Indian, Alaska Native, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander patients had the lowest screening rates throughout the study period. Patients aged 30 to 49 years and non–English-speaking patients consistently had the highest CCS rates across all years. Patients in the Western and Southern census regions had lower CCS rates than those in other regions. Conclusions and Relevance In this cross-sectional study of patients with at least 1 health care encounter in an EMR system, all CCS rates increased across all racial and ethnic groups from 2019 to 2024, with the greatest gains observed among Hispanic patients. However, persistent disparities remained, particularly among American Indian, Alaska Native, Native Hawaiian, and Pacific Islander patients and those in the Western and Southern regions. These findings suggest that although screening uptake has improved over time, substantial geographic and racial and ethnic disparities in CCS persist, highlighting important areas for future research and intervention efforts.

item.title: Organ Preservation and Quality of Life After Total Neoadjuvant Treatment in Rectal Cancer
item.dc:creator: Markus Diefenhardt
Emmanouil Fokas
Rebekka Kosmala
Bülent Polat
Christoph Thomas Germer
Anke Schlenska-Lange
Thomas Kuhnt
Michael Ghadimi
item.description:
Authors: Markus Diefenhardt, Emmanouil Fokas, Rebekka Kosmala, Bülent Polat, Christoph Thomas Germer, Anke Schlenska-Lange, Thomas Kuhnt, Michael Ghadimi, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639063
Abstract: Importance Data on quality of life (QOL) after total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) are important for counseling patients on the benefits of watch-and-wait (WW) vs total mesorectal excision (TME) for rectal cancer. A thorough understanding of both options and their long-term impact on bowel, urinary, sexual function, and other QOL domains remains limited. Objective To examine the association of organ preservation with QOL and functional outcomes among patients with rectal cancer treated in 2 phase 2 clinical trials. Design, Setting, and Participants This unplanned, post hoc, cohort study used data from the CAO/ARO/AIO-12 and CAO/ARO/AIO-16 trials, recruiting participants from June 15, 2015, through October 7, 2020, from 19 centers in Germany. Included patients had cT3 to cT4 or node-positive rectal adenocarcinoma. Total neoadjuvant treatment included chemoradiation therapy combined with induction or consolidation chemotherapy. The statistical analysis was performed from March 6 to December 23, 2025. Main Outcomes and Measures The association of WW with functional outcomes and QOL was assessed using prospectively recorded EORTC QLQ-C30, EORTC QLQ-CR29, and Wexner score questionnaires. Differences in QOL scores were estimated using adjusted longitudinal and cross-sectional analyses with a predefined clinically meaningful difference of at least 5 points. Results Baseline questionnaires were available from 346 of 385 eligible patients (89.9%; median [range] age, 60 [19-80] years; 257 male [67%]), while available QOL questionnaires decreased over time to 185 (48.1%) at 5 years. Using the longitudinal analytic approach, statistically significant and clinically meaningful differences in favor of WW were noted for fecal incontinence (−21.2 [95% CI, −30.0 to –12.3]; P &amp;lt; .001); stool frequency (−19.8 [95% CI, −27.6 to −11.9]; P &amp;lt; .001); embarrassment (−17.0 [95% CI, −27.4 to −6.6]; P = .002); flatulence (−15.2 [95% CI, −24.4 to −6.0]; P &amp;lt; .001), buttock pain (−11.9 [95% CI, −20.8 to −3.0]; P = .01); social (9.7 [95% CI, 1.1-18.3]; P = .03), physical (10.2 [95% CI, 4.1-16.3]; P = .002), and role (13.9 [95% CI, 4.9-22.9]; P = .003) functioning; and global health status (9.2 [95% CI, 3.2-15.2]; P = .004). These clinically meaningful differences were detectable in both the intended organ preservation and disease-free groups. Patients with sustained clinical complete response at 3 years (n = 29) vs those with pathologic complete response or matched baseline characteristics favored WW for fecal incontinence (−24.0 and −11.6, respectively), stool frequency (−34.6 and −19.1), sore skin (−18.0 and −18.1), buttock pain (−14.7 and −17.6), embarrassment (−41.1 and −20.5), role functioning (19.1 and 10.9), and social functioning (20.0 and 8.4). Conclusions and Relevance In the absence of prospective randomized trials, this study provides evidence suggesting long-term clinically meaningful benefits for organ preservation regarding QOL, especially for most gastrointestinal subscales, social functioning, and global health status, over a 5-year period among patients with rectal cancer. As treatment options for patients with rectal cancer now routinely include WW in cases of clinical complete response after TNT, patient-reported QOL measures have become paramount for informed shared decision-making. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifiers: NCT02363374 and NCT03561142

item.title: Disparities in α <sub>1</sub> -Antitrypsin Deficiency Testing and Treatment in US Adults
item.dc:creator: Arianne K. Baldomero
Lisa Smith
Amy Gravely
Vickram Tejwani
Chris H. Wendt
item.description:
Authors: Arianne K. Baldomero, Lisa Smith, Amy Gravely, Vickram Tejwani, Chris H. Wendt
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639328
Abstract: Importance α 1 -Antitrypsin deficiency (AATD) is underdiagnosed despite guidelines for broad testing, and the factors associated with low testing and treatment are not well known. Objective To identify factors associated with low AATD testing and augmentation therapy in individuals with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and asthma. Design, Setting, and Participants This is a retrospective, multicenter cohort study using national electronic health record data from the Veterans Health Administration from January 1, 2020, to December 31, 2024. Data analysis was conducted from July to October 2025. Participants were individuals with a diagnosis of COPD and/or asthma (≥2 International Classification of Diseases, Ninth Revision, or International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision codes). Exposure Individual demographics, comorbidities, tobacco use, rural-urban residence, Social Vulnerability Index (SVI), and drive time to the specialty care facility. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcomes were prevalence of and factors associated with AATD testing and augmentation therapy prescription. Multivariable regression models were used, adjusting sequentially for demographics, comorbidities, tobacco use, rural-urban residence, SVI, and drive time to the specialty care facility. Results Among 2 384 913 individuals with COPD and/or asthma (mean [SD] age, 64.2 [14.3] years; 178 898 female [7.5%]; 16 778 [0.7%] American Indian or Alaska Native; 14 996 [0.7%] Asian; 331 202 Black or African American [15.3%]; 19 029 [0.9%] Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander; 1 787 951 White [82.4%]), 138 278 (5.8%) underwent testing. In fully adjusted models, cirrhosis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 6.40; 95% CI, 6.29-6.51) and bronchiectasis (aOR, 3.73; 95% CI, 3.59-3.87) were associated with higher odds of testing. Older ages and active tobacco use were associated with lower odds of testing. Rural-urban residence and SVI had similar odds across categories. Longer drive times were associated with progressively lower odds of testing (&amp;gt;90 vs ≤30 minutes; aOR, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.62-0.65). Of 8564 with AATD diagnosis, 320 (3.7%) were prescribed augmentation therapy and showed a similar pattern as testing, occurring less often among patients from minoritized racial and ethnic groups, those actively using tobacco, and those with longer drive times to specialty care, and more often among those with cirrhosis and bronchiectasis. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study of individuals with COPD and/or asthma, AATD testing and augmentation therapy were profoundly low. System-level reform is needed to bridge gaps across age, comorbidities, tobacco use, and health care access.

item.title: Prehospital Point-of-Care GFAP for Detection of Intracranial Hemorrhage in Acute Nontraumatic Coma
item.dc:creator: James Price
Kate Lachowycz
Gabriel Palti
Charlotte Wright

Sabina Zylyftari

item.description:
Authors: James Price, Kate Lachowycz, Gabriel Palti, Charlotte Wright, Rob Major, Sabina Zylyftari, Christian Foerch, Ed B. G. Barnard
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639337
Abstract: Importance Rapid identification of intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) in patients with acute nontraumatic coma is critical to guiding triage and early management; however, prehospital diagnostic tools remain limited. Objective To evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of prehospital whole-blood point-of-care measurement of glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and ubiquitin carboxy-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCH-L1) for detecting ICH. Design, Setting, and Participants This diagnostic study used data collected by a UK physician-paramedic helicopter emergency medical service between January 1, 2025, and April 30, 2026. A consecutive sample of adult patients (aged ≥16 years) presenting with acute nontraumatic coma, defined as Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of 12 or less, who underwent prehospital rapid sequence induction (RSI) of anesthesia with clinical suspicion of ICH were eligible for inclusion. Patients with traumatic pathology and those without follow-up data were excluded. Patients were observed for up for 30 days from hospital admission. Data analysis was performed in June 2026. Exposure Prehospital whole-blood point-of-care brain biomarker (GFAP and UCH-L1) testing using the i-STAT Alinity Point-of-Care Blood Analyzer (Abbott Laboratories). Main Outcome and Measures Diagnostic accuracy of GFAP and UCH-L1 for detecting ICH, using computed tomography as the reference standard. Sensitivity, specificity, predictive value, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were calculated. Results The primary study cohort comprised 65 patients who underwent prehospital brain biomarker testing (median age, 63 [IQR, 47-69] years; 55.4% male). The median (IQR) GCS score was 4 (3-6). ICH was present in 50.8% (n = 33). Thirteen (20.0%) patients underwent neurosurgery, and the 30-day survival rate was 46.2% (n = 30). GFAP demonstrated high sensitivity (97.0%; 95% CI, 84.2%-99.9%) and discriminatory ability (AUC, 0.94; 95% CI, 0.87-0.99). UCH-L1 showed lower sensitivity (78.8%; 95% CI, 61.1%-91.0%) and specificity (18.8%; 95% CI, 7.2%-36.4%), with limited discriminatory performance. A combined biomarker approach achieved 100.0% sensitivity (95% CI, 89.4%-100.0%) and a negative predictive value of 100.0% (95% CI, 47.8%-100.0%). Conclusions and Relevance In this diagnostic study of adults with acute nontraumatic coma undergoing prehospital RSI, point-of-care prehospital GFAP testing was feasible and demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy in detecting intracranial hemorrhage. Further prospective external validation is required to determine its association with triage, treatment decisions, and patient outcomes.

item.description:
Authors: Varun Nandakumar, Yeonjung Jo, Micah Ostrowski, Georges Gebrael, Zeynep Irem Ozay, Edwin Lin, Krishnam Goel, Rachel Revillo, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2639276
Abstract: Importance Lutetium Lu 177 vipivotide tetraxetan (Lu-177) prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) is a targeted radioligand therapy approved for patients with metastatic androgen pathway modulator–resistant (mAPMR) prostate cancer after progression on androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs). Data to guide treatment sequencing are limited. Objective To evaluate survival outcomes in patients with mAPMR prostate cancer receiving Lu-177 PSMA by line of therapy and the timing of taxane exposure. Design, Setting, and Participants This cohort study used a deidentified electronic health record research database to obtain comprehensive longitudinal oncology data from community and academic practices across the US. Among patients with metastatic prostate cancer in the dataset, those who received Lu-177 PSMA after an ARPI between December 19, 2018, and June 23, 2025, met the inclusion criteria. The data cutoff was June 30, 2025. Exposure Receipt of Lu-177 PSMA, stratified by line of therapy and timing of taxane exposure (before Lu-177 PSMA, after Lu-177 PSMA, or never received taxane). Main Outcomes and Measures Primary end points were clinical time to next treatment (TTNT; defined as the time from Lu-177 PSMA initiation to next systemic therapy or death) and clinical overall survival (OS; defined as the time from Lu-177 PSMA initiation to death). Both outcomes were censored at last follow-up and estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method with 95% CIs. Results Among the 850 patients included, the median (IQR) age was 74 (68-80) years; most were treated in community settings (598 [70.4%]) and had commercial insurance (520 [61.2%]). A total of 466 patients (54.8%) received taxane before Lu-177 PSMA, 35 (4.1%) received taxane after Lu-177 PSMA, and 349 (41.1%) never received taxane. Median clinical TTNT and clinical OS with Lu-177 PSMA were 8.0 (95% CI, 7.4-9.0) months and 12.0 (95% CI, 11.0-13.0) months for patients with taxane exposure before Lu-177 PSMA; 10.0 (95% CI, 9.2-11.0) months and 14.0 (95% CI, 13.0-17.0) months for patients who never received taxane; and 6.0 (95% CI, 4.9-8.0) months and 16.0 (95% CI, 13.0–not reached) months for patients with taxane exposure after Lu-177 PSMA, respectively. Conclusions and Relevance In this cohort study, outcomes with Lu-177 PSMA were broadly consistent across treatment lines and taxane sequencing groups. These findings may help inform patient counseling, although prospective studies are needed to determine the optimal treatment sequencing strategy.

Jorge Otero

item.description:
Authors: Sònia Anglès-Acedo, Inmaculada Alonso, Laura Ribera-Torres, Eduard Mension, Jorge Otero, Carolina Herranz-Diez, Ramon Farré, Natalia Castrejon, et al.
Journal: JAMA Network Open; Volume: 9; Issue: 10; Pages: e2638937
Abstract: Importance Laser therapy is increasingly used to treat genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) in breast cancer survivors, but sham-controlled evidence of benefit remains limited. Objective To evaluate 12-month efficacy and safety of fractional carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) laser therapy (CLT) vs sham laser therapy (SLT) for GSM in breast cancer survivors receiving aromatase inhibitors. Design, Setting, and Participants This is a secondary analysis of a single-center, double-blind, sham-controlled randomized clinical trial conducted at a tertiary academic hospital in Spain. Participants included breast cancer survivors with GSM and dyspareunia receiving aromatase inhibitors, recruited from October 30, 2020, to September 1, 2021. Participants were followed up for 12 months. Data were analyzed from December 1, 2024, to June 30, 2025. Intervention Five monthly sessions of CLT or SLT plus first-line nonhormonal therapy (FLT), including vaginal moisturizers and vibrators. Main Outcomes and Measures The primary outcome was the between-group difference in change in Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI) score. Secondary outcomes included rate of sexual activity, dyspareunia, Spanish Body Image Scale, quality of life (12-Item Short Form Health Survey), Vaginal Health Index, objective parameters (pH, vaginal maturation index, epithelial measures), serum estradiol level, FLT adherence, and adverse events. Results Of the 84 randomized participants (mean [SD] age, 53.8 [8.8] years), 67 completed the 12-month follow-up (CLT, 32; SLT, 35). The CLT group did not differ from the SLT group in FSFI score change from baseline to 12 months (difference, CLT vs SLT, −0.69 [95% CI, −3.58 to 2.20]; P = .64), nor in any secondary outcome. Across the full sample, significant improvements from baseline to 12 months were observed in FSFI score (18.9 to 23.0; mean difference, 4.5 [95% CI, 3.1-5.9]; P &amp;lt; .001), dyspareunia (mean difference, −3.7 [95% CI, −4.4 to −3.0]; P &amp;lt; .001), Spanish Body Image Scale (mean difference, −3.9 [95% CI, −5.1 to −2.8]; P &amp;lt; .001), and Vaginal Health Index (mean difference, 4.2 [95% CI, 3.1-5.2]; P &amp;lt; .001). Sexual activity increased among 57 of 67 participants (85.1%; odds ratio, 2.35 [95% CI, 1.23-4.50]; P = .009). Improvements were found in pH (mean difference, −0.5 [95% CI, −0.8 to −0.2]; P &amp;lt; .001) and vaginal maturation index (mean difference, 19.0% [95% CI, 13.4%-24.5%]; P &amp;lt; .001). FLT adherence was similar between groups. No severe adverse effects occurred. Conclusions and Relevance In this randomized clinical trial of breast cancer survivors receiving aromatase inhibitors, vulvovaginal CLT provided no additional benefit for sexual or vaginal health at 12 months. Improvements in both groups likely reflected FLT adherence, trial participation, or contextual factors rather than laser efficacy. High-quality sham-controlled trials remain essential before routine implementation. Trial Registration ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04619485

item.title: Socioeconomic Inequality and Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events
item.dc:creator: Cæcilie Stilling Denholt

Kathrine Kold Sørensen
Marcella Broccia
Kristian Kragholm
Thomas Alexander Gerds
Christian Torp-Pedersen
